newsitem.title: CYPRUS: US envoy says no imminent Cyprus crisis.
newsitem.headline: US envoy says no imminent Cyprus crisis.

text.p: A U.S. envoy said on Monday there was no "crisis issue" in Cyprus because the government had assured him it would not bring any part of a controversial anti-aircraft missile system to the divided island for at least 16 months.
Turkey had threatened military action several times last week to stop deployment of the S-300 anti-aircraft missiles, which the Cypriot government announced last week it would acquire from Russia.

U.S. State Department official Carey Cavanaugh said he had not asked Cypriot President Glafcos Clerides to cancel the purchase, which was criticised by Washington, but had been assured during their one-hour meeting it would not be deployed soon.

"What he (Clerides) did do though, and I find this very helpful, is he gave us assurances that not a single component of those missile systems will be brought to this island in the next 16 months," Cavanaugh said.
"I believe this should effectively defuse this as a crisis issue for Cyprus. People should not now be talking of concerns of conflict because that is not a problem of today," he said.
